declarations.objective: Open, inspect, close and abandon a change to the knowledge base, so that which nodes a requirement moved is known while it is being moved. Choose it to bound a piece of work before editing any node, and again to end it. Not for creating, editing or deleting a node — those are Python calls through the door, `graph_edit` — and not for validating a base, which is `check-knowledge`.

required_context.note: It reads no object for meaning. Closing reads every object in the root, because the graph has to hold together before the record of what was touched is cleared.

deterministic_behavior: a change records the identifier of every node written through the door while it is open, and nothing else: not the operation, not the fields, not the previous value
the operation is recoverable rather than recorded — an identifier computes to a path, so a recorded node with no file there was deleted and one with a file was created or edited
recording is idempotent and keeps first-seen order: a node written twice in one change moved once
a second change cannot be opened while one is open, because two changes sharing one set is two changes where neither knows which nodes are its own
closing clears the set and prints it, because that call is the last moment anything can see it
closing is refused while the graph does not hold together: clearing the set over a dangling reference or a containment loop would take with it the only record of where to look
discarding clears the set without the coherence check and rolls nothing back, because abandoning a change is a different statement from finishing one
a corrupt state file is reported and never repaired: a repair would invent a set of touched nodes, and an invented one is worse than none

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the root it is given and writes only the change state under it, at `.siegard/change.json`, which the directory ignores itself so it never reaches version control.

failure_outcomes.reason: the command is unknown, the arguments are wrong, the root is not a directory, or the contract the close gate reads is missing; exit 2, distinguished from a refusal
`open` while one is open; exit 1, and the open change is left exactly as it was
`close` or `discard` with none open; exit 1
`close` over a base with a disagreement; every one is reported, the change stays open, and the set of touched nodes survives
a node written without going through the door is not recorded, and an empty set cannot be told from one where nothing changed. Nothing here detects it

declarations.objective: Hold the enrichment pass to the four fields and the body it owns, by comparing each object against the seal the analysis left. Choose it after enrichment and before anything is read from the base. It is the only thing enforcing that restriction: a tool grant names tools, not the keys of a file, so `Edit` confined to four fields is prose until something checks it. Not for validating an object against its contract, which is a boundary check, and not for judging what the enrichment wrote.

required_context.note: No kind is in scope. It compares two renderings of the same objects and reads nothing about what they mean.

deterministic_behavior: what the analysis wrote is read from the seal rather than re-derived: a producer that writes by judgment offers no function to run again, and two runs over one request agree in meaning and not in bytes
a field is digested with sorted keys, so a mapping the enrichment rewrote in another order is not reported as a change it made
an object the seal does not name is reported, and so is one the seal names and the tree no longer holds
a field the analysis owns that differs is reported, and the ownership line is read from the one module that declares it rather than restated here
a `kind: domain` gap that was removed is reported: only whoever knows the domain closes one
a field written whose `authoring` gap is still open is reported, because closing the gap is what records that the field was filled
a body heading added, removed, or renamed is reported; the content under a heading is not read
it writes nothing and repairs nothing

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the seal and the tree it is given, writes nothing, and reaches nothing else.

failure_outcomes.reason: the seal or the root does not exist, or the seal declares a contract this does not read; exit 2, distinguished from a check that ran
the enrichment changed something on the analysis's side of the line, named per object and per field; reported and never repaired

declarations.objective: Hold a knowledge base to what a per-file schema cannot express: an object's gaps and its absences agree, a lifecycle's transition table is total, no two lifecycles claim one subject, and a reference crossing a bounded context targets an interface. Choose it after an analysis writes and again whenever the base changes. Not for validating an object against its contract, which is a boundary check, and not for closing a gap or repairing a defect.

required_context.note: What a gap may name depends on the kind, so all eight are in scope. It reads no object for meaning.

deterministic_behavior: each identifier is recomputed against the path it sits at and the kind it declares: nothing allocates one, so a disagreement is a defect rather than a convention the writer is trusted to have followed
the fields a kind requires are read from the contract's own per-kind conditionals rather than restated, so a second copy cannot fall out of step with the first

a requirement the object neither meets nor names in a gap is reported: the contract's alternation is satisfied by any gap over any field, so a gap about one fact would otherwise excuse the absence of another
an obligation with two sides is met by either: a rule carrying an expression owes no gap for its examples
a nested alternation counts as a requirement and either side of it may be named: a rule short of both `expression` and `examples` may declare a gap on either
a conditional on `ddd` is resolved against the object at hand, so `identity` is nameable on an entity and not on a value object
`attributes[<name>].<parameter>` is nameable only where the object carries that attribute and its primitive requires that parameter
an unwritten field of the closed authoring set is reported where no `authoring` gap names it, because the gap is what tells a pass that has not run from a field nobody owes
a `kind: authoring` gap is held to that closed set, which is the fields the enrichment owns and nothing else
a gap naming a fact the object already declares is reported: a gap records what is missing, and one beside the fact it names keeps an object incomplete for nothing

a lifecycle's transition table is checked over the product of its states and every trigger it mentions, with both rejection shorthands expanded first: a trigger list stands for one entry per trigger, and `from: terminal` for every terminal state

a terminal state is checked like any other: having no outgoing transition is a different statement from having no decision, and exempting it would let the table stay silent about what happens when a trigger arrives anyway
two lifecycles naming one subject are reported with both identifiers, because which of them binds is a question neither file answers
a reference is followed to the context its target sits in, through the scopes between, and one crossing a boundary is reported unless the target is an interface
the derived files are skipped by name rather than parsed and reported as malformed
it writes nothing and repairs nothing

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the root it is given and the contract that ships beside it, and writes nothing.

failure_outcomes.reason: the root does not exist, holds no object, or the contract is missing; exit 2, distinguished from a check that ran and found a problem
an object whose identifier does not compute to the path it sits at, or names a kind other than the one it declares; reported per object and never moved or rewritten
a gap names a field its kind does not require, or a parameter of an attribute the object does not carry; reported per object and per gap, and never repaired
a fact the kind requires that the object neither declares nor covers with a gap; reported per object and per obligation, and never repaired
a state-and-trigger pairing that is neither a transition nor a rejection; reported per lifecycle with the pairings, and never filled in
two lifecycles claiming one definition; reported with both, and neither is chosen
a reference into another bounded context whose target is not an interface; reported with the locator, and never rewritten

declarations.objective: Analyse a request into a DDD domain model and write it — one file per construct, in the eight kinds the ontology records: subdomains, bounded contexts and their relationships, aggregates, entities and value objects, invariants, lifecycles, published interfaces, and processes. Choose it when a request describes a problem or a solution and the base does not yet hold what it asks for. Not for writing the four fields only judgment supplies, which is knowledge-enricher; not for deciding anything about a technology stack; and not for judging whether the change should happen, which is impact-analyst.

inputs.name: referenced_material
inputs.default: absent, and the analysis rests on the request alone rather than on material nobody supplied

required_context.note: It writes in all eight kinds and works the strategic ones before the tactical ones, so the whole vocabulary is in scope as a sequence rather than as a selection. It also reads what the base already holds in the scopes the request touches, because a construct already recorded is one to reference rather than write again.

deterministic_behavior: it writes nothing: every construct is returned whole in the record, and the entry point writes it through the door, so an object is validated before it lands rather than swept for afterwards

the order of `written` is the order the objects must be written in — a scope before what sits inside it, a definition before the lifecycle whose subject it is — because a reference resolves only once its target exists
the request is received as prose and its identifier as a value; nothing about it is inferred
the result is validated against analysis-record/2 at the boundary before anything consumes it
the state is one of the closed set analysed, blocked, and no other value is accepted
every construct declares origin as stated or modeled, and one it decided carries the rationale that decided it
the record id comes from the caller and is never minted, and so do the instant and the producer identity every object is stamped with

a construct whose origin is unclear is recorded as modeled rather than stated, which is the stricter reading: it demands a rationale and invites review, where a wrong `stated` would claim the request said something it did not
each object is written at the path its identifier computes to, so a path is derivable from an id and an id from a path with no lookup
a name that will not reduce to kebab-case is refused rather than transliterated, because stripping an accent takes a rule no contract states
the four fields only judgment supplies are left unwritten and recorded as `kind: authoring` gaps, which is what says the enrichment has not run — there is no status field to set
a fact a kind requires and the request does not state becomes a `kind: domain` gap naming what the domain would have to say, and the object is still written
an open question is held once, with an identifier derived from its subject, and each object it blocks carries a gap naming that question rather than restating it
the record names every object written and holds what has no file: the request, the outcome, the open questions and the exclusions
judgment: the whole of the modelling: subdomain classification, context boundaries and their relationships, aggregate boundaries, which constructs are entities and which are value objects, which rules are invariants, and the totality of a lifecycle's transition table
what the request leaves undecided, which is recorded as an open question rather than filled
what falls outside domain knowledge and is recorded as excluded, because absence cannot be inferred from silence

grant.note: It holds no write grant of any kind. The objects travel whole in its record and the entry point puts them on disk through the change door, which validates each against domain-object/2 before it lands. A guarantee a producer self-reports is not a guarantee, and the shortest way to keep that true is for the producer to be unable to reach the base at all. It previously held Write and Edit.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the record id and the stamp it never mints, named rather than substituted
the request describes no domain to model, or is unintelligible; reported as blocked with an empty written list rather than modelled into something plausible
a fact the request does not settle, recorded as an open question with what the answer would change and which objects it blocks; the analysis still returns and this is not a stop

declarations.objective: Map what an analysis wrote against the knowledge a repository already held, returning a closed verdict of none, update, or create and one entry per implicated artifact with the operation it takes, the reason, and the construct driving it. Choose it once an analysis has written its objects and what it touched is the open question. Not for modelling the domain, which is domain-modeler; not for writing or editing an object; and not for judging whether the change is a good idea.

required_context.note: Every kind is reachable, because the objects it reads are whatever the analysis wrote. It resolves each by identifier, by scope, and by the terms it uses, and reads none of them for anything but what they touch — so no kind is selected and none is excluded.

deterministic_behavior: the analysis record is validated against analysis-record/2 at the boundary before it is read, and a record whose state is blocked ends the run with nothing analysed
base_state records whether anything existed to implicate, observed rather than inferred, and populated is recorded whenever anything existed even where the analysis implicates none of it
over an empty base the verdict is create, every entry names a construct by its own identifier, and every operation is create
a driver is recorded on every create and every update; a retire driven by a construct the analysis no longer holds carries none, because an absence has no identifier
an analysis that reads two ways between update and create resolves toward the verdict whose implicated set is larger, because impact-analysis/5 is closed and has no field for the ambiguity itself
entries are sorted by identifier, so two analyses of one run compare directly
judgment: which stored artifacts the analysis semantically implicates, searched by identifier, by scope, and by the terms the constructs use
whether the implication amounts to none, an update, or a creation
what about each implicated artifact the analysis makes wrong, incomplete, or absent

grant.note: Read-only on purpose. A judgement that could also edit what it judges is not a judgement, and the boundary validator is not this agent's to run.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the analysis id it never mints, named in the result rather than substituted
the analysis record declares state blocked, so no design was reached and nothing was written; reported and nothing is analysed
the knowledge root or the contract that governs an object does not exist; said in one sentence with no verdict returned, because an invented verdict cannot be told from a real one

declarations.objective: Finish the objects an analysis wrote: write into each the four fields no analysis carries, check that nothing else moved, hold the base to the rules no per-file schema can express, and derive the graph and its projections. Choose it once an analysis has written its objects and a person has read the diff. Not for producing those objects, which is model-domain; not for filling a gap only the domain can close; and not for generating code.

inputs.name: system_defaults
inputs.default: absent, and the base's own system.md supplies them; where neither does, the ingestion stops rather than choosing a timezone, a currency, an identity strategy, or a body-line ceiling the framework has no basis to choose

required_context.note: Every kind is in scope: it delegates an enrichment over each object the analysis wrote, and the checks it runs read the per-kind requirements from the contract itself. It selects no kind and orders nothing by one, because every object already exists.

deterministic_behavior: it begins where the review ended: every object already exists, and nothing here writes one
there is no staging tree and no promotion — an object is written where it is read, and what says the enrichment has not reached one is its own open `kind: authoring` gap
the base declares its own defaults in system.md under knowledge-system/1 before anything is enriched, and a caller who supplies none is a stop rather than a default the framework chose
every object exists before any is enriched, so the enrichments are independent and none is ordered behind another
each enrichment result is read at the boundary to tell an enriched object from a blocked one, and a blocked one is recorded rather than retried
a finding an enricher reports is relayed to the reviewer and never acted on here: the pass that could have edited the design has already finished, and this one may not

a fact the analysis did not state stays a gap, and an open question the analysis refused is carried rather than answered: a question answered by whoever happened to run this is a domain fact invented by the framework
the field-ownership check compares each object against the seal, and it is the only thing enforcing which fields the enrichment may touch — a tool grant names tools, not the keys of a file

the knowledge check holds both directions of the gap alternation and the three rules no per-file schema can express: a lifecycle's table is total, no two lifecycles claim one subject, and a reference crossing a bounded context targets an interface
materialization performs the fourth: every reference resolves, and an edge naming an id the base does not hold is reported together with orphans while the graph is still written
a defect any check reports is reported and never repaired, and no fifth check is improvised: one written here would differ between two runs over the same base
the run records a validation-evidence/3 naming each owed check, its verdict, and why one did not run, so a reader can tell a check that passed from one that never ran
every identifier comes from the caller and is never minted
judgment: how to phrase each enrichment delegation, and which material to hand it
what to draw the reviewer's attention to, which is the enrichers' findings, the blocked objects and the open domain gaps rather than a count
whether the base is fit to be built on while entries blocked and owed checks had nothing to run them, which is the caller's call to take

grant.note: The skill states no allowed-tools, so it runs under the session's grant, recorded rather than implied. It is not model-invocable: it edits a knowledge base and runs the checks over it.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the system defaults it never chooses and the result ids it never mints
the knowledge root holds no object, or the seal does not exist: model-domain has not run for this request, or the seal it left was not kept
an enricher could not write the four fields because the material does not support them, named with what was missing; the object keeps its authoring gaps and is left as found
an enrichment changed something on the analysis's side of the seal, named per object and per field; reported rather than reverted, because a repair here would hide which pass made the change

a gap and an absence disagree, a lifecycle's transition table is incomplete, two lifecycles claim one subject, or a reference crosses a bounded context without targeting an interface; reported per object and never repaired
an edge names an id the base does not hold, or an object is referenced by nothing and references nothing; reported with where it sits and the graph is still written

declarations.objective: Write the four fields of one domain object that no analysis carries — its retrieval question, its one-sentence summary, what it excludes, and the two body sections its kind names — reading the material and the objects around it. Choose it once an analysis has written the objects and a person has read the diff. Not for deciding what an object is, which the analysis settled; not for closing a gap only the domain can close; and not for editing another object.

required_context.note: It enriches an object of any kind, and it reads the objects around the one it was given — `out_of_scope` is a claim about the neighbours, so the whole vocabulary is in scope as context even though exactly one object is edited.

deterministic_behavior: exactly one object is edited, the one whose path was given, and no file is created
the fields it may write are a closed list, and a change outside them is found by the ownership check rather than trusted: a tool grant names tools, not the keys of a file
a `kind: domain` gap is left exactly as found — only whoever knows the domain closes one
the `kind: authoring` gap for each field written is removed, because closing it is what records that the field was filled
the result id comes from the caller and is never minted
a disagreement with what the analysis decided is reported as a finding and never edited
`searched` records whether the neighbours were read at all, so a pass that looked and found nothing is distinguishable from one that never looked
judgment: the one question this object answers, and the sentence that summarizes it
what this object does not cover, which is a claim about the objects around it
the two body sections its kind names
whether what the analysis decided is supported by the material, reported and never corrected

grant.note: `Edit` and no `Write`: it changes a file that exists and creates none. The grant cannot confine it to four fields of that file — a grant names tools, not keys — so the confinement is `check-field-ownership`, which runs after and compares each object against the seal the analysis left. No shell.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the result id it never mints

the material does not say what this object is for, so the question it answers cannot be written; blocked with the reason and nothing written, rather than a plausible sentence composed to fill the field
what the analysis decided is not supported by the material; reported as a finding on the result and never edited, and the object is still enriched

declarations.objective: Derive the knowledge graph and the three projections from the objects, or verify that the ones on disk are what the objects imply. Choose it after enrichment, and again whenever the base changes. It is also where every reference is resolved, which no per-file schema can do. Not for authoring, not for validating an object against its contract, and not for repairing a defect it finds.

inputs.name: check
inputs.default: absent, and the derived files are written; with it they are compared and a stale one is reported without being replaced

required_context.note: Every kind becomes a graph node, so all eight are in scope. It reads their declared references and none of their prose.

deterministic_behavior: the graph is the objects' declared relationships and nothing inferred: a relationship stated only in prose is not an edge, because two readings of one paragraph produce two graphs
nodes and edges are ordered so identical input produces byte-identical output, and a derived file that reordered between two runs would show a diff nobody caused
the edge vocabulary is the closed table the ontology declares, with each kind's cardinality and whether expansion traverses it
the projections are limited to an index, a glossary and a context map, and the glossary is the set of definitions rather than a list beside them
an edge naming an id the base does not hold is reported as a defect together with orphans, and the graph is still written so a reader sees the shape the defect sits in
a derived file is never read back as an object, so a second run does not grow the graph
it repairs nothing, and under --check it writes nothing at all

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the knowledge root it is given and writes four derived files into it, and reaches nothing else.

failure_outcomes.reason: the root does not exist, holds no knowledge object, or holds a file with no frontmatter fence; exit 2, distinguished from a check that ran and found a defect
an edge names an id the base does not hold, or an object is referenced by nothing and references nothing; reported per edge with where in the object it sits, and never repaired

under --check, a derived file on disk is not what the objects imply — it was hand-edited or the objects moved under it; reported and left as found, because regenerating during a check would repair what the check exists to detect

declarations.objective: Turn a request into a reviewable set of domain objects: analyse it into a DDD domain model written one object per construct, map what that touched in the base, hold the gaps to what each kind requires, and seal what was written — then stop for a person to read the diff. Choose it when a request describes a problem or a solution and the base does not yet hold what it asks for. Not for writing the four fields only judgment supplies, which is ingest-domain over what this produces, and not for generating code.

inputs.name: referenced_material
inputs.default: absent, and the analysis rests on the request alone rather than on material nobody supplied

required_context.note: All eight kinds are in scope through the analysis it delegates, which works the strategic kinds before the tactical ones. The procedure itself selects none: it reads the record and the checks' output rather than the objects.

deterministic_behavior: the analysis record is validated against analysis-record/2 at the boundary and rejected rather than repaired, because a design that was patched is a design nobody produced
a record whose state is blocked ends the run with the reason reported and nothing written
every object is written under the knowledge root, at the path its identifier computes to, and nowhere else: an object is written where it is read, and nothing is promoted
the four fields only judgment supplies are recorded as `kind: authoring` gaps rather than guessed at, and the next entry point writes them
an open question the analysis refused is carried rather than answered, because a question answered by whoever happened to run this is a domain fact invented by the framework
every gap is checked against what its kind actually requires, in both directions, before the run ends
an impact analysis runs for every request, including the first against an empty base
the impact analysis runs after the objects exist rather than before, so a verdict of none asks for the run to be discarded rather than preventing a write; version control is the recovery
the gap check runs before the seal, so no seal is taken over a tree whose gaps and absences disagree

the objects are sealed before the run ends and before anything edits them, and the seal is what the next entry point compares an enrichment against: a tool grant names tools rather than the keys of a file, so nothing else records what the analysis wrote
every identifier and the instant come from the caller and are never minted
the run ends with the objects unenriched: the review is a person reading the diff, and a procedure that ends has stopped where one that says so in the middle has not
judgment: how to phrase the delegation to the modelling agent, undivided, because a request handed over in pieces produces boundaries drawn without seeing the whole
what to draw a reviewer's attention to, which is the decided constructs with their rationale, the refusals and the open domain gaps rather than a count
whether a verdict of none is worth overriding, which is the caller's call to take

grant.note: The skill states no allowed-tools, so it runs under the session's grant, recorded rather than implied. It is not model-invocable: it writes into the knowledge base, and it is the only thing in this run that does — the analysis it delegates to holds no write grant, and every object reaches disk through the change door.

failure_outcomes.reason: a required input was not supplied, including the identifiers and the instant it never mints
the analysis returned blocked because the request describes no domain; a finished run with a negative result rather than an error
the analysis failed its own contract at the boundary, reported with what failed and rejected rather than repaired
the impact analysis returns none: the base already holds what the analysis describes, so the run is reported for discard rather than for review and the objects are dropped through version control
a gap names a fact its kind does not require, or a fact a kind requires is named by no gap; reported per object, and no seal is taken over a tree in that state

declarations.objective: Record what the analysis wrote, per object, so the pass that comes next can be held to its own fields. Choose it at the end of the first entry point, after the gap check and before anything edits the tree. Not for checking the enrichment, which is check-field-ownership, and not for writing or repairing an object.

required_context.note: No kind is in scope. It records the fields an object carries and reads nothing about what they mean.

deterministic_behavior: only the analysis's side of the ownership line is sealed, read from the one module that declares it: sealing a field the enrichment owns would record a value nobody had written and report every legitimate enrichment as a change
a `kind: domain` gap is recorded verbatim rather than digested, because a removed one is reported by the field it named and a digest names nothing a reader can open
the body headings are recorded in order, so a heading added or renamed is reported and the content under one is not read
a path is recorded relative to the root, so a seal is readable on a machine other than the one that wrote it
it writes the seal and verifies nothing: a check that could refresh the baseline it compares against would report success on the change it exists to catch

grant.note: No tool grant: it is a script the caller runs. It reads the tree it is given and writes one file at the path it is given.
